transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what finally scared me into actually making the appointment is, I’ve been having these thoughts like, if I didn’t wake up tomorrow, maybe that would be easier. I don’t mean I want to hurt myself—I don’t, really—but the thought keeps showing up, and it made me think maybe I shouldn’t just keep brushing it off.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities?

Yeah… I have. I mean, I still try. I’ll put my paints out on the table, or I’ll tell myself I’m going to go to pottery class, because that used to be my little reset, you know? I even bought this really nice blue glaze once—well, I guess that’s not really the point.

But when I’m actually there, I just kind of sit and look at the clay or the brushes, and there’s just… nothing. Like the spark I used to get from it isn’t there. It feels strange, because I know I used to love it.
How long have you been feeling this way, and do you notice that your mood has been consistently low or depressed most days?

Most mornings lately, yeah… I wake up and it’s like this heavy, gray feeling is already there, before I even get dressed for the store. It’s funny, I used to be so particular about what blouse I wore to work—customers notice those things, you know—but lately it’s like the color has drained out of everything before the day even starts. So… yes, I’d say my mood has been pretty low most days.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not good enough, even when there’s no real reason to feel that way?

Yes… I do. It’s silly, probably, but I’ll get stuck replaying these tiny things from work. Like if a display sign was a little crooked, or one of the new trainees looked confused after I explained something, I’ll go home and think, “Well, that’s because I’m useless as a supervisor.”

And then I’ll start remembering every other time I didn’t handle something perfectly. I mean, retail is always messy—people move things, customers ask the same question three different ways, and the seasonal aisle never stays neat, not even for an hour—but somehow I make it about me. Like I should’ve done better, even when it’s not really a big deal.
How long have these feelings of low mood, loss of interest, and guilt been going on?

I think… about six months, give or take. It’s hard to pin down exactly because it didn’t arrive all at once, you know? It was more like my morning walks stopped helping, and then pottery class felt like another thing on the calendar instead of something I looked forward to.

I remember thinking maybe it was just a bad week at work, or the weather, or that I needed to reorganize the kitchen cabinets—because I do that when I’m trying to feel in control—but no, the low, flat feeling has been there for months now. Around six months, I’d say.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like waking up much earlier than you used to or having trouble falling asleep?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, sleep is… I’ve never been one of those people who just puts their head down and disappears for eight hours. My sister can do that, which always amazed me—she could nap through the vacuum cleaner.

Lately, I don’t know that I’ve noticed a clear pattern like waking up at some exact awful hour or anything. Some nights I lie there thinking about little things, but then I’ll also get distracted by whether I remembered to put the laundry in the dryer, or what time the store delivery comes in, and it’s hard to say if that’s “trouble sleeping” or just me being me.

So… I guess I haven’t really tracked it. Nothing jumps out as a big change, I don’t think.
Have you had any other periods in your life where you felt this way before, or is this the first time you’ve experienced these feelings?

I don’t know… I’m not sure I can say cleanly. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, like anyone has, and sometimes I’ll think, “Was that the same thing?” But then I start comparing it to, you know, when my kids were younger or when work was especially hectic, and it gets all tangled up.

There were times I felt worn down, sure, but whether it was this same kind of low, flat feeling… I’m not really sure. I’d have to think about it more.
Can you recall if there was a time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks in a row?

I’m trying to think… more than two weeks in a row is such a specific cutoff, isn’t it? I mean, I know I’ve had times where I felt off or sort of uninterested, but then I’ll remember some birthday dinner or some thing at work that seemed okay, and then I start doubting my own memory.

There were stretches, maybe, but I can’t honestly say, “yes, that was more than two weeks,” not with any confidence. I don’t keep track of moods the way I keep track of sales reports or appointments. So… I’m not sure. I don’t really have a clear one I can point to before this.
Can you think of any time in your life before this current six-month period when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had thoughts like you’re not good enough for a period of two weeks or more?

I really can’t pin one down. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt badly about myself or wasn’t enjoying much, but then I think about all the normal ups and downs—work stress, family stuff, getting older, even just bad weather for a week—and it blurs together.

Two weeks or more… I honestly don’t know. Nothing before this stands out clearly enough for me to say yes, that was definitely the same kind of thing.
Can you think of any time in your life before this current six-month period when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had thoughts like you’re not good enough for a period of two weeks or more?

I know you’ve asked it a couple times, and I’m sorry, I’m not trying to dodge it. I just… I can’t think of a clean example from before this.

There were periods where I was tired or kind of discouraged, but life was busy, you know? In retail there’s always some season that wipes you out—holidays, inventory, someone quitting right before a big weekend—and then at home there’s always something too. So I have trouble separating “I was stressed and worn out” from “I was really down for two weeks.”

So… no, I don’t have a clear time before this six months that I can point to and say that was definitely it.

Looking back over your life, can you think of any time before this current six-month period when you had a clear stretch of at least two weeks where you felt down most days, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, and maybe felt guilty or not good enough?

I’m sorry, I know I’m probably circling the drain on this, but I still don’t have a clear example. When I look back, I can remember being unhappy here and there, or just kind of worn thin, but then my mind goes off to what was happening at the time—like whether the store was short-staffed, or if I was just tired from all the running around.

So as far as a definite two-week stretch where I felt down most days and wasn’t interested in things, before these last six months… I really can’t say yes. I don’t remember it clearly enough to give you that.

Looking back over your life, even if it wasn’t recent, can you think of any time when you had a clear stretch of at least two weeks where you felt down most days, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, and felt guilty or not good enough?

I still can’t really pull up an old stretch clearly, not in the way you’re asking. What I can say is that lately, most mornings, I wake up with this heavy gray feeling, like the color’s already drained out of the day before I even get dressed for the store.

And then I start thinking about the day ahead—who’s scheduled, whether someone’s going to call out, all that—and I sort of get carried off into that. But before this current period, a definite two weeks like that… I just don’t know.

Looking back over your life, even if it wasn’t recent, can you think of any time when you had a clear stretch of at least two weeks where you felt down most days, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, and felt guilty or not good enough?

I know, and I’m sorry, I keep ending up in the same place with this. I can think of times I was unhappy or tired or felt like I wasn’t keeping up, but then I start thinking about the details—like work schedules, and who was managing what, and whether it was around the holidays—and I lose the thread.

So… a clear two-week stretch from earlier in my life where it was like that most days? I can’t really give you one. I’m not saying it absolutely never happened, just that I don’t remember anything clearly enough to say yes, that was it.
Can you think of any time before these last six months when you had a period of feeling down, losing interest in things, or feeling guilty that lasted for at least a couple of weeks?

I’m not really able to pin one down before these last six months. I mean, I can remember feeling low here and there, or guilty about not handling things better—especially with work, because retail can just eat up your whole brain if you let it—but then I start thinking, was that really a couple weeks, or was it just a bad patch because inventory was a mess or someone quit?

So… no, I don’t have a clear period from before that I can say lasted at least a couple of weeks in that way.

Looking back over your life, can you think of any time before these last six months when you had a clear period of at least two weeks where you felt down most days, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, and felt guilty or not good enough?

I’m sorry, I know you’re asking it very clearly, and I keep circling around it. Before these last six months… I just don’t have a clean memory of a two-week stretch like that.

There were times I felt lousy or like I wasn’t doing enough, but then I start attaching it to work—holiday rush, staffing problems, all the usual store chaos—and I can’t honestly say, yes, that was most days for two weeks and I lost interest in things. I just don’t remember it clearly enough to give you that.

Looking back over your life, can you think of any time before these last six months when you had a clear period of at least two weeks where you felt down most days, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, and felt guilty or not good enough?

I don’t think I can give you a clear yes on that. I’ve had times where I felt kind of worn down or disappointed in myself, sure, but when I try to look back and make it into a neat two-week period, it gets fuzzy.

And honestly, some of it all blends together with work stuff—retail schedules, people calling out, holiday crowds, all of that. I remember being tired and frustrated, but I can’t really separate out whether I was down most days and not enjoying things for two full weeks. So… before these last six months, I don’t remember a clear stretch like that.

Looking back over your life, even if it wasn’t recent, can you think of any time when you had a clear stretch of at least two weeks where you felt down most days, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, and felt guilty or not good enough?

Lately, yes… I mean, not really looking back years ago, but lately most mornings I wake up and it’s like this heavy gray feeling is already there. Like the color’s drained out of everything before I even get dressed to go to the store.

And then I start thinking about opening routines and whether someone called out, and I know that’s not exactly what you asked, but it’s all mixed together in my head. The clearest thing I can say is that lately, the mornings have felt really down like that.

Looking back over your life, even if it wasn’t recent, can you think of any time when you had a clear stretch of at least two weeks where you felt down most days, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, and felt guilty or not good enough?

I know you’re asking if it happened sometime way back, but the clearest thing I can point to is more recent. Most mornings lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, like everything’s already sort of drained of color before I even get dressed for the store.

And then my mind goes right to the store schedule and who’s going to be late, and I get off track thinking about that, but… the mood part, the down feeling, that’s been there in the mornings.

Looking back over your life, can you think of any time before these last six months when you had a clear stretch of at least two weeks where you felt down most days, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, and felt guilty or not good enough?

Before the last six months… I’m still not coming up with a clear example. I mean, I’ve had rough patches, sure—especially around busy seasons at the store, when everything feels like it’s piling up and you’re just trying to get through the day.

But if you’re asking for a definite two weeks where I was down most days, stopped enjoying things, and felt guilty or not good enough… I don’t really know. I can’t point to one and say yes, that was definitely it. It’s more fuzzy than that.
